name: Balancer v2 Composable Stable Pool rounding exploit (mainnet leg)
chain: ethereum (mainnet leg only; Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Polygon, Gnosis also hit)
verdict_reason: On the Ethereum mainnet leg no bot or whitehat front-ran an attacker tx. Every replay of the attacker calls (Bitfinding 0x5af00b07 = the whitehat that returned ~$964K; plus searcher/copycat EOAs) lands in a LATER block than the attacker tx on the same pool: Bitfinding 1 block after A1 (23717398 vs 23717397), 4 blocks after A3, 3 blocks after A9. The call data is a confirmed adaptation (A1 creation input vs Bitfinding input: 3 of 983 32-byte words differ, all address constants), so the "front-ran the attacker" wording in the Balancer post-mortem (as quoted by AMBCrypto) is a post-inclusion replay/rescue of the residual pool balances, not a pre-emption of a pending attacker tx. A1 and most attacker txs never appeared in the public mempool; the only public pending ones (A8-A9b) were not pre-empted. Same-block activity before/after the attacker is arbitrage backrunning (0xc0ffee445a22 at idx 2 paying 20.6 ETH to the builder).

replay_evidence.summary: tx 0x1dc60f91 (block 23717398 idx 2) is a contract-creation tx whose input is the attacker A1 input (0x6ed07db1, block 23717397 idx 1) with 3 of 983 32-byte words changed: word 1 (beneficiary address: attacker 0xaa760d53... -> 0x5af00b07...) and words 895-896 (owner address 0x506d1f9e... -> 0x5af00b07...). Same length (31,427 bytes). Everything else, including the attacker EOA2 address constant 0x766a892f8b..., is byte-identical. Call tree is the same shape (12 Vault staticcalls, 2 batchSwap-selector calls, 2 manageUserBalance calls; 121 + 103 Swap events vs 121 + 105 for A1) on the same two pools (0xdacf5fa1... osETH/WETH, 0x93d19926...). The next tx in the bundle (idx 4) withdraws WETH/wstETH from the Vault internal balance of the new contract to the EOA.
replay_evidence.diff_artifact: computed in this run from site/raw/rpc-balancer2025/tx_<hash>.json inputs (not a separate file)

bots.ordering: Attacker A1 lands in block 23717397 (slot 12944332, 07:46:47 UTC) at idx 1; Bitfinding bundle lands in the NEXT block 23717398 (slot 12944333, 07:46:59 UTC) at idx 2-4 with 2 gwei priority; A1 was not in the public mempool dump, nor were Bitfinding txs. The copy is a post-inclusion replay, 1 block (12 s) later.
bots.notes: Same pattern repeated against EOA1 wave 2: 0xa4ee77db (block 23717631) copies A3 0x8e260bf8 (block 23717627), 4 blocks later; 0xed0c8654 (23717709) copies A9 0x2a0ead4e (23717706), 3 blocks later. Never earlier than the attacker tx on the same pool. Funds returned to the DAO multisig; 10 % bounty paid 2026-01-15.

auction.summary: Titan (extraData) built the attack block 23717397 and the Bitfinding block 23717398 (the latter delivered by bloXroute regulated from an unlabelled builder pubkey 0x88a53ec4...); the attack tx paid ~0 tip (3.9e-5 gwei) yet sat at idx 1 behind a 7-wei self-send, with the Titan fee-recipient collecting a 20.6 ETH backrun payment at idx 2 while only 0.0502 ETH reached the proposer (Ultra Sound). Bitfinding paid 2 gwei priority (0.058 ETH total). Next-block winner 18.169 ETH via bloXroute regulated. No builder refunds to a bot were observed. Winning block of 23717397 is not in the retained bids (Ultra Sound history aged out), so when the attack tx first reached the builder is unknown.

tests.test: Real attacker identified incl. several EOAs, contracts, deployment, reverted/late txs
tests.detail: EOA1 0x506d1f9e + EOA2 0x766a892f, one beneficiary 0xaa760d53; deployment = A1 (constructor exploit); no reverted attacker txs.

tests.test: Bot tx from a different address whose call tree replays the attacker victim calls, SAME OR EARLIER block
tests.detail: Replays exist (Bitfinding, 0x7bb28442, 0x87a16382, others; 3 of 983 words differ) but every one lands in a LATER block than the attacker tx on the same pool (1, 2, 3, 4 blocks later).

tests.test: Bot tx pre-empted a still-pending attacker tx
tests.detail: Only A8, A8b, A9, A9b were public (mempool-dumpster first-seen 7.4-18.7 s before the timestamp of the including block); no exploit-shaped tx on those pools precedes them (pool-sequence scan blocks 23717390-23718400). A1-A7 and EOA2 txs are absent from the dumpster (private flow), so no public pending window exists to pre-empt.

headline_text: Balancer v2 mainnet: whitehat Bitfinding replayed the attacker's exploit input one block after it landed, rescued about 260 ETH-equivalent in this tx, and returned it to the DAO; a 10% bounty was paid on 2026-01-15.

harmonized.verdict_reason: Every replay (Bitfinding whitehat 23717398; copiers) landed AFTER the attacker's tx 23717397 on the same pool: post-inclusion rescue of residual balances, not pre-emption.
